# tests/fixtures/gh/ — manifest

Hand-written `gh` fixtures that back the bats suite. Each fixture pairs with a
sibling `<name>.schema.json` capturing the **shape** (key paths and value
types) of real `gh` output for the equivalent `--json` query.
`tests/test_fixture_contract.bats` enforces that every key path used in a
fixture is present in its schema — so the next time `gh` evolves or a fixture
is hand-edited with a hallucinated key, CI fails instead of silently
green-lighting a broken predicate (see GH#8 for the canonical near-miss).

Schemas are regenerated by `tests/fixtures/gh/refresh.sh` against
`$LOOP_FIXTURE_REPO` (default: `aniryou/loop`). Run it any time you change
the `--json` field set on a runner query, or when CI's
`LOOP_FIXTURE_LIVE=1` test reports drift.

Last refreshed: **2026-05-07** (against `aniryou/loop`).

## Fixture map

| Fixture | Source `gh` command (production) | Scenario |
|---|---|---|
| `issues-high.json` | `gh issue list --repo $REPO --state open --label severity:high --json number,assignees,labels --limit 50` | Two unassigned + one assigned; backs `eligibility_dev_count` and the assignee filter test in `test_eligibility.bats`. (No `labels` field — exercises the "permissive when label absent" path.) |
| `issues-medium.json` | `gh issue list --repo $REPO --state open --label severity:medium --json number,assignees,labels --limit 50` | Different unassigned numbers from `issues-high.json` so the union-with-overlap test exercises `sort -u`. |
| `issues-with-locks.json` | `gh issue list --repo $REPO --state open --label severity:high --json number --limit 50` | Four issue numbers (101–104) used by the lock-dir post-filter test. Number-only shape (no `assignees`). |
| `issues-with-blocked-label.json` | `gh issue list --repo $REPO --state open --label severity:medium --json number,assignees,labels --limit 50` | Three unassigned issues; one without `blocked:human` (201) and two with (202, 203). Backs the GH#28 label post-filter tests. |
| `prs-current.json` | `gh pr list --repo $REPO --state open --search "head:dev-agent/ -is:draft" --json number,headRefOid,reviews,statusCheckRollup --limit 100` | One PR whose `[reviewer-agent: clean]` review is *newer* than the head commit; the `eligibility_review_pending` jq filter must filter it OUT. (Pre-GH#26 this query also requested `commits`; that field was dropped because `commits + reviews + --limit 100` blew past the GraphQL 500k-node ceiling on repos with ≥10 dev-agent PRs. The head commit's `committedDate` is now resolved via a separate `gh api graphql` call per `headRefOid` and injected into the filter via a `$dates` map. GH#46 added `statusCheckRollup` so the predicate can gate on in-flight CI without spawning the orchestrator LLM.) |
| `prs-stale.json` | (same command) | One PR whose `[reviewer-agent: changes]` review is *older* than the head commit; the filter must INCLUDE it. |
| `prs-mixed.json` | (same command) | Three PRs covering current/stale/no-reviews so the filter returns 2. All three carry a completed `statusCheckRollup` so the GH#46 CI gate passes them through to the review-coverage filter. |
| `prs-dispatch.json` | `gh pr list --repo $REPO --state open --json number,headRefName,isDraft,mergeable --limit 100` | Six PRs covering every dispatcher branch: `dev-agent/*` non-draft / draft / conflicting, plus `feature/*` to verify branch-prefix filtering. |
| `pr-followup.json` | `gh pr view <N> --repo $REPO --json reviews,comments` | Single PR (object root, not array) with one `[reviewer-agent: changes]` review newer than one `🤖 Developer agent` comment. Bats tests mutate the body/timestamps to cover every verdict (`clean`/`nits`/`comment`/`changes`/`blocked`) and the dev-comment-newer-than-review case for `eligibility_followup_pr`. |
| `pr-merger.json` | `gh pr view <N> --repo $REPO --json reviews,comments,commits,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,headRefOid,isDraft` | Single PR (object root) primed for merge: `[reviewer-agent: clean]` review covers head, no human follow-up, `mergeable=MERGEABLE`, `mergeStateStatus=CLEAN`. Bats tests mutate verdict / timestamps / commit oid / mergeStateStatus to cover the skip and human-veto branches in `eligibility_merge_pr`. |

## Schema notes

- Schemas use a flat dict shape: `{ "<jq-path>": "<type-union>" }`.
  - Path syntax: `.` for the root, `[]` for "any element of this array",
    `.foo` for an object field — so `.[].reviews[].submittedAt`.
  - Type names are jq's: `null`, `boolean`, `number`, `string`, `array`,
    `object`. Multiple types observed at the same path are joined with `|`.
- Schema source uses `--state all` and drops the `--label` filter so even
  repos where a label is currently empty still produce a representative
  schema. The fixture's *production* command is the column above; the
  schema-source command is encoded in `refresh.sh`.
- `null` in a fixture is always tolerated: scenarios often stub fields with
  `null` to scope what's relevant. The contract still rejects (a) keys not
  present in the schema (a hallucinated field) and (b) non-null types the
  schema doesn't list (e.g. a `string` where real gh always returns a
  `number`).

## Refresh workflow

```bash
# Default — regenerate schemas against aniryou/loop
tests/fixtures/gh/refresh.sh

# Dry-run — emit schemas to stdout, leave tests/fixtures/gh/ untouched
tests/fixtures/gh/refresh.sh --print

# Different source repo. Should be a "rich" repo: at least one assigned
# issue + one PR with at least one review, so nested keys like
# `.[].assignees[].login` and `.[].reviews[].submittedAt` show up.
LOOP_FIXTURE_REPO=octocat/hello-world tests/fixtures/gh/refresh.sh

# Live contract test — runs refresh.sh and asserts no git diff
LOOP_FIXTURE_LIVE=1 bats tests/test_fixture_contract.bats
```

### Source-repo contract & union-merge

`refresh.sh` is **read-only** (only `gh ... list` / `gh ... view`); it never
mutates the source repo. It is also **monotonic**: each run union-merges the
freshly-derived schema with the existing on-disk schema (per path: union of
types, deduped, sorted, rejoined with `|`). Consequences:

- Running it twice in a row produces no `git diff`.
- Running it against a *sparser* `LOOP_FIXTURE_REPO` than was used previously
  also produces no diff — previously-recorded paths survive.
- The only diffs you'll see are when real `gh` surfaces a new key the schema
  doesn't already know about, which is the drift CI should flag.

The union-merge is a defensive backstop, not a substitute for using a rich
source repo. If `LOOP_FIXTURE_REPO` has zero PRs or zero assigned issues, the
*initial* schema generation against it will undercount nested keys; the
union-merge only helps once those keys have been recorded at least once
(typically by an earlier run against `aniryou/loop`).
